rationale: The packet establishes the Part I Section A.1 table structure (lbs/day and mg/l columns, each split into 30-Day Average and Daily Maximum) and shows that Total Suspended Solids at Outfall 001 has N/A in both lbs/day columns, Report in the mg/l 30-Day Average column, and the numeric value 50 in the mg/l Daily Maximum column. It also shows that other pollutants in the same table use Report, N/A, and numeric values in different column combinations. However, the packet does not include permit language defining what Report or N/A denote in discharge-limitation cells, nor any explicit rule that a lone numeric value in the mg/l Daily Maximum column establishes an enforceable limit when the paired mg/l 30-Day Average cell says Report and both lbs/day cells say N/A. The included footnotes address BMP/discharge restrictions and WET testing, not table notation semantics. Without grounded definitions of these conventions or an explicit enforceability statement tied to this row, neither ACCEPT (that 50 is an enforceable limit for compliance comparison) nor REJECT (that it is not) can be established from the available evidence. Per P5, unsupported uncertainty is preferred to unsupported semantic closure.
